doc.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023

title: Getting gigs in New York by word of mouth
summary: Bailey says careers are word of mouth, and being good on the gig matters more than social media clips.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: How do you get — speaking of gigs — if you want to play at Smoke’s or any number of places, how do you do that? I mean I have this vision of so many jazz musicians in New
York City and the chance of getting into some of the better clubs must be very competitive.

Well you know I mean the thing about, I mean it doesn’t have to be jazz, but you’re only as good as your last gig. It’s word of mouth. Your career is word of mouth. You’re on a gig, someone hears you and they love the way you play. They love the way you sound. They love your attitude. And then you get the calls. And then you’re a sideperson or you start to develop something. And that’s really how it goes. I mean you know this is a kind of a funny age where with some of the younger kids they’re coming up in this idea that they have an Instagram or a TikTok post and they can play something for 20 seconds. Like — well how do you sound on a gig? Can you play on it? Do you know tunes? All those things count. So I think that’s really how you build your career is through what you’re doing right now.
